title: Grid Illumination
description:
# Grid Illumination

You are given an `n x n` grid. Every cell may contain a lamp, and all lamps are initially off except the positions listed in `lamps`.

Each `lamps[i] = [row_i, col_i]` turns on the lamp at that cell. If the same lamp position appears more than once, it still represents one active lamp.

An active lamp illuminates every cell in its row, every cell in its column, and every cell on both diagonals passing through it.

For each query `queries[j] = [row_j, col_j]`, return `1` if that cell is currently illuminated, otherwise return `0`. After answering the query, turn off every active lamp in the 3 x 3 block centered on the queried cell, including the queried cell itself. Lamps outside the grid are ignored.

## Example 1:

**Input:** n = 5, lamps = [[0,0],[4,4]], queries = [[1,1],[1,0]]
**Output:** [1,0]
**Explanation:** The first query is lit by both lamps, then it turns off the lamp at `[0,0]`. The second query is not lit.

## Example 2:

**Input:** n = 5, lamps = [[0,0],[4,4]], queries = [[1,1],[1,1]]
**Output:** [1,1]
**Explanation:** The first query turns off `[0,0]`, but `[4,4]` still illuminates `[1,1]` diagonally.

## Example 3:

**Input:** n = 5, lamps = [[0,0],[0,4]], queries = [[0,4],[0,1],[1,4]]
**Output:** [1,1,0]
**Explanation:** Query `[0,4]` is lit and turns off that lamp. Query `[0,1]` is still lit by `[0,0]`, then turns off `[0,0]`.

## Constraints:

* `1 <= n <= 10^9`
* `0 <= lamps.length, queries.length <= 20000`
* `0 <= row_i, col_i, row_j, col_j < n`

solutions.name: Four Counter Maps with Packed Active Lamps
solutions.description:
## Approach
Store active lamp positions in a `HashSet<Long>` and keep four counter maps for rows, columns, main diagonals, and anti-diagonals. A query is illuminated when any of its four line counters is positive. After answering, scan the query cell's 3x3 neighborhood and remove any active lamp found there, decrementing all four counters.

## Key Insight
The grid can be as large as 10^9 by 10^9, so the state must be sparse. Illumination depends only on four line identifiers: `row`, `column`, `row - column`, and `row + column`.

## Complexity Analysis
Each unique lamp is inserted once, and each query checks four counters plus at most nine cells. The time complexity is O(L + Q), where L is the number of lamp entries and Q is the number of queries. The active set and counters use O(L) space.

solutions.name: Unified Encoded Line Counter
solutions.description:
## Approach
Use one `HashMap<Long, Integer>` for all illuminated lines. The key combines a line type with the line value, so rows, columns, diagonals, and anti-diagonals share the same counter structure. Active lamps are still kept in a packed-coordinate set for exact duplicate and shutoff handling.

## Key Insight
The four counter maps in the standard solution differ only by line identity. Encoding `(lineType, lineValue)` into a long keeps the same logic while reducing repeated map plumbing.

## Complexity Analysis
Lamp insertion, query checks, and neighborhood removal are constant work per lamp or query. The time complexity is O(L + Q), and the line counter plus active set use O(L) space.

solutions.name: Line Membership Sets
solutions.description:
## Approach
Instead of storing integer counters for each line, store the active lamp keys that belong to every row, column, and diagonal. A query is illuminated when any of its four line sets exists and is non-empty. Removing a lamp deletes the same key from all four line sets.

## Key Insight
Set-backed lines avoid duplicate-count and decrement mistakes because each active lamp contributes one key to each line. This is especially useful for teaching why duplicate lamp positions must be ignored.

## Complexity Analysis
Every unique lamp key is inserted into four sets and removed from four sets at most once. Queries inspect four sets and nine possible lamps, so the time complexity is O(L + Q). The line membership maps use O(L) space.

solutions.name: Coordinate-Compressed Line Arrays
solutions.description:
## Approach
Collect every row, column, and diagonal value that can be queried or updated, assign each value a compact index, and store line counts in arrays. Active lamps remain packed in a set so neighborhood shutoff is exact. This keeps sparse grid logic but replaces repeated counter-map lookups with array indices.

## Key Insight
Only lines touched by lamps or queries can matter. Compressing those line identifiers preserves the sparse model while making the four illumination checks plain array reads.

## Complexity Analysis
Building the compression maps and processing all operations are linear in the number of lamps and queries. The time complexity is O(L + Q), and the compressed arrays and maps use O(L + Q) space.

solutions.name: Row-Bucket Active Lamp Map
solutions.description:
## Approach
Keep illumination counters for the four line families, but store active lamps as `row -> set of columns` instead of a packed coordinate set. When a query shuts off its 3x3 neighborhood, look up each candidate row bucket and remove the column if it exists.

## Key Insight
The shutoff operation is local by coordinates, so row buckets provide an exact active-lamp membership test without relying on a combined long key. The same line counters still answer illumination in constant time.

## Complexity Analysis
Each lamp is inserted once and removed at most once. Each query checks four counters and at most nine row-bucket positions. The time complexity is O(L + Q), and the row buckets plus counters use O(L) space.
